Understanding a breathing reading

Many healthy adult dogs breathe fewer than 30 times per minute during sleep. A sleeping rate below 20 can also be normal. Calm-awake readings can be higher, so compare readings taken in the same state.

Ceva’s Cardalis guidance advises contacting your vet if the sleeping rate is above 30 breaths/min or rising over time. This is a reason to seek advice, not a diagnosis. Follow the monitoring instructions your vet gives for your dog.

If your dog is struggling to breathe, seek urgent veterinary care. Do not wait to finish a count.

The reference above does not set your dog’s threshold. Pawbreath uses only the threshold you enter and does not adjust it for breed, size, sex or neuter status.

Sources: Ceva / Cardalis monitoring guidance, healthy-dog sleeping-rate study, and VCA home breathing guidance. Reviewed 13 November 2026. Source links need an internet connection; this guidance is available offline.
